data.one_liner: Widgets and addons for Cached Query in Flutter including query and mutation builders.
data.what_it_does: Provides Flutter-specific builders and configuration extensions for Cached Query. It allows refetching queries automatically on app resume or when connection is re-established, and supplies QueryBuilder, InfiniteQueryBuilder, and MutationBuilder widgets.
use_when: You are already using Cached Query for server state management in Dart.
You need UI builders like QueryBuilder or MutationBuilder for your queries.
You want automatic query refetching on app resume and connectivity changes.
avoid_when: You are not using Cached Query.
You want a general-purpose state management solution like Bloc or Riverpod without caching server data.
strengths: Seamlessly integrates Cached Query with Flutter widgets.
Automatic refetching on resume and network change via connectivity_plus.
Works well alongside other state management patterns like the bloc pattern.
weaknesses: Tight coupling to the Cached Query ecosystem.
Requires additional configuration compared to standalone state managers.
data.setup_notes: Configure CachedQuery with configFlutter instead of config, and optionally initialize CachedStorage.

alternatives.name: flutter_bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a full-fledged event-driven state management architecture rather than dedicated query caching.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want compile-safe global state management with built-in family and caching capabilities.

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a simpler dependency injection and state propagation tool.
